results.input: Specification-driven development and AI-assisted requirements workflows: GitHub Spec Kit, OpenSpec, and related primary documentation. Focus on traceability, change control, validation, and executable specifications.

output.authoritative_sources: [GitHub Spec Kit Repository](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) | [OpenSpec Documentation (Intent-Driven Development)](https://intent-driven.dev/knowledge/openspec/) | [GitHub Blog: Spec-driven development with AI](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/generative-ai/spec-driven-development-with-ai-get-started-with-a-new-open-source-toolkit/)
output.caveats: AI-driven specification systems can lead to "reward-hacking" if convergence criteria are too loose or if the agent prioritizes passing checks over functional correctness. The "Source of Truth" approach requires high discipline to prevent a single specification file from becoming a monolithic, unmanageable document. Executable specifications are only as effective as the underlying AI's ability to interpret natural language without introducing ambiguity.
output.recommended_skill_changes:
`clone-to-platform-pipeline` Add a "Platform Constitution" step to define invariant architectural rules that the cloned system must converge toward during its evolution.
`clone-to-platform-pipeline` Implement a "Delta Spec" workflow for tracking modifications made to the original clone, ensuring each change is traceable to a specific platform requirement.
`dh-method-competitive-intelligence` Integrate the "Idea Assessment" workflow (Intake, Research, Define, Shape, Decide) to formalize the transition from market research to actionable product specifications.
`skill-creator` Adopt the "Specify-Plan-Tasks-Converge" loop to ensure new skills are defined by observable behavior contracts before implementation.
`skill-creator` Add a requirement for "Architectural Decision Records" in the skill definition phase to document the rationale for specific tool choices or logic flows.
output.research_lane: Specification-driven development and AI-assisted requirements workflows: GitHub Spec Kit, OpenSpec, and related primary documentation. Focus on traceability, change control, validation, and executable specifications.
output.verified_practices: Specifications must be treated as the primary, executable source of truth where code serves the specification rather than the other way around (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md). Proposed modifications should be captured as "Delta Specs" (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED) to ensure clarity for both humans and AI agents before merging into a unified "Source of Truth" (https://intent-driven.dev/knowledge/openspec/). Implementation plans should explicitly map every architectural decision and technology choice back to specific requirements in the core specification to ensure traceability (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md). Automated convergence checks should be used to audit the codebase against the spec and plan, identifying implementation gaps as new tasks (https://github.github.com/spec-kit/quickstart.html). Durable Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) must be maintained alongside functional specs to preserve the reasoning behind technical choices across the system's lifecycle (https://intent-driven.dev/knowledge/openspec/).

results.input: Modern product discovery and product-management practice: continuous discovery, opportunity-solution trees, assumptions testing, and outcome-oriented roadmaps. Use original authors or official practitioner documentation where possible.

output.authoritative_sources: [Product Talk by Teresa Torres](https://www.producttalk.org/getting-started-with-discovery/) | [SVPG Product Discovery by Marty Cagan](https://www.svpg.com/product-discovery/) | [ProductSide Outcome-Based Roadmaps](https://productside.com/guide-to-outcome-based-product-roadmaps/)
output.caveats: Continuous discovery requires a dedicated product trio (Product, Design, Engineering) to be fully effective, which may exceed the scope of solo agent execution. Outcome-based frameworks depend on pre-defined, measurable business metrics that might not exist for experimental or early-stage platform builds.
output.recommended_skill_changes: `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Integrate an Opportunity-Solution Tree phase to map target application features to underlying customer outcomes before beginning platform architecture. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence`: Add a Competitive Opportunity Mapping step to identify unmet needs by treating competitor features as specific solutions within a broader problem space. `skill-creator`: Mandate a Riskiest Assumption Test (RAT) for every new skill to verify environment feasibility and user desirability before full implementation.
output.research_lane: Modern product discovery and product-management practice: continuous discovery, opportunity-solution trees, assumptions testing, and outcome-oriented roadmaps.
output.verified_practices: Teams should maintain a minimum of weekly customer touchpoints to sustain a continuous discovery cadence and avoid building based on stale data (https://www.producttalk.org/getting-started-with-discovery/). Use Opportunity-Solution Trees to visually link business outcomes to specific customer pain points and proposed solutions, ensuring strategic alignment (https://www.producttalk.org/opportunity-solution-tree/). Deconstruct every solution into five assumption categories—desirability, viability, feasibility, usability, and ethical—to identify hidden risks (https://www.producttalk.org/five-types-of-assumptions/). Prioritize testing by mapping assumptions on a 2x2 grid of importance versus evidence, focusing resources on high-importance/low-evidence risks first (https://www.producttalk.org/assumption-testing/). Replace feature-based timelines with 'Now, Next, Later' roadmaps that focus on achieving specific behavioral outcomes rather than fixed delivery dates (https://productside.com/guide-to-outcome-based-product-roadmaps/).

results.input: Responsible competitive intelligence and lawful software reverse engineering: public observation, interoperability, copyright/trade-secret limits, provenance, and clean-room practice. Prioritize government, legal, or recognized standards sources.

output.authoritative_sources: [EU Directive 2009/24/EC](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32009L0024) | [EFF Coders' Rights Project Reverse Engineering FAQ](https://www.eff.org/issues/coders/reverse-engineering-faq) | [Lexology: IP Clean Room Policy Guide](https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=57ce5c16-717f-4fe0-9925-30628c54085c) | [SCIP Code of Ethics](https://www.scip.org/page/Ethical-Intelligence)
output.caveats: Clean-room practices do not provide a defense against patent infringement claims, only copyright and trade secret theft. Legal protections for interoperability are strictly limited to functional necessity and do not permit the reproduction of creative expression.
output.recommended_skill_changes: `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Implement a mandatory provenance logging system that tracks every functional requirement back to its public source or interoperability specification. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence`: Add a "Public Observation Audit" phase that verifies all data sources are accessible via proper means without bypassing technical protection measures. `skill-creator`: Revise the analysis module to output only functional specifications, explicitly prohibiting the inclusion of original code snippets in the design phase. `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Enforce a two-agent architecture where the "analyst" agent and "builder" agent are prohibited from sharing raw source code context.
output.research_lane: Responsible competitive intelligence and lawful software reverse engineering: public observation, interoperability, copyright/trade-secret limits, provenance, and clean-room practice.
output.verified_practices: Reverse engineering is legally protected for the purpose of achieving interoperability between independently created programs (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32009L0024). A "clean-room" process must separate the "dirty" analysis team from the "clean" development team to prevent the transfer of protected expression (https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=57ce5c16-717f-4fe0-9925-30628c54085c). Practitioners must accurately disclose their identity and organization before conducting competitive intelligence interviews (https://www.scip.org/page/Ethical-Intelligence). Information obtained via decompilation must be strictly confined to parts necessary for interoperability and cannot be used to market a substantially similar program (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32009L0024). Thorough provenance documentation of the independent development process is required to provide a defense against trade secret misappropriation (https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=57ce5c16-717f-4fe0-9925-30628c54085c).

results.input: Software quality and non-functional requirement practice: accessibility, privacy/security, performance, resilience, and usability acceptance criteria. Prioritize W3C, NIST, OWASP, and similarly authoritative sources.

output.authoritative_sources: [W3C WCAG 2.2 Accessibility Guidelines](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) | [OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)](https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/) | [NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 2 Cyber Resiliency](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/160/v2/r1/final) | [Google SRE Service Level Objectives](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/)
output.caveats: Compliance with these standards varies by industry and jurisdiction, particularly regarding legal accessibility requirements like the ADA or EAA. Security practices must be scaled based on the data sensitivity and risk profile of the specific application. Performance targets are highly dependent on user expectations and hardware constraints.
output.recommended_skill_changes: `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Insert a mandatory "NFR Hardening" phase after cloning to implement OWASP ASVS Level 2 security controls and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence`: Add an "NFR Benchmarking" module to the discovery phase to evaluate competitors' accessibility scores, security header strength, and error-handling resilience. `skill-creator`: Revise the skill template to require the definition of "Acceptance Criteria" grounded in ISO/IEC 25010 quality characteristics, including specific SLIs for performance and reliability. `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Integrate automated accessibility testing for new WCAG 2.2 criteria, such as minimum target size (24x24px) and focus visibility, during the platform evolution step. `skill-creator`: Incorporate a "Cyber Resiliency" design pattern into the architecture phase, mandating strategies for system anticipation, withstanding, and recovery based on NIST SP 800-160.
output.research_lane: Software quality and non-functional requirement practice: accessibility, privacy/security, performance, resilience, and usability acceptance criteria.
output.verified_practices: Interactive elements must maintain a minimum target size of 24x24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing to prevent accidental activation by users with motor impairments (https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/new-in-22/). Applications should utilize parameterized queries and contextual output encoding to prevent OS command and SQL injection vulnerabilities as defined by ASVS Level 2 (https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/). Systems must be engineered to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions using techniques like segmentation and redundancy to ensure cyber resiliency (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/160/v2/r1/final). Performance management requires defining Service Level Objectives (SLOs) that set clear user expectations for latency and availability while utilizing error budgets to balance stability and innovation (https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/). Accessibility compliance now requires that focused components are not obscured by author-created content like sticky headers or footers (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/). Software quality evaluation should categorize properties into characteristics such as performance efficiency, reliability, and functional suitability to ensure comprehensive usability acceptance (https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso-iec:25010:ed-1:v1:en).

results.input: Agent-skill or procedural-instruction authoring: progressive disclosure, compact guidance, testability, evaluation, versioning, and reusable resources. Prioritize official tool-provider or open standards documentation.

output.authoritative_sources: [Skill authoring best practices - Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices) | [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills - Anthropic Engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills) | [AI agent evaluation: frameworks and metrics that go beyond the benchmarks - Algolia](https://www.algolia.com/blog/ai/ai-agent-evaluation-frameworks-metrics-testing-strategies) | [Model Context Protocol Specification - Versioning](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/learn/versioning)
output.caveats: These practices assume an agentic environment with filesystem access and code execution capabilities. Performance improvements depend heavily on the underlying model's reasoning capacity and context window management. Semantic versioning for skills is a community-driven recommendation rather than a strictly enforced protocol in all frameworks.
output.recommended_skill_changes: `skill-creator`: Enforce a 500-line limit for the primary SKILL.md file and mandate the use of domain-specific sub-files for advanced technical details. `skill-creator`: Integrate a mandatory YAML frontmatter check requiring gerund-based naming (e.g., 'processing-data') and third-person descriptions to ensure discovery compatibility. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence`: Refactor the procedural workflow into a progressive disclosure model, moving deep analysis templates into a separate 'REFERENCE.md' file. `clone-to-platform-pipeline`: Implement a 'Low Freedom' instruction block for fragile database migration steps while maintaining 'High Freedom' for creative architecture design. `skill-creator`: Add a 'Testability' section that requires authors to provide at least three representative evaluation tasks and a chain-of-thought reasoning rubric. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence`: Adopt YYYY-MM-DD versioning in the skill metadata to track backwards-incompatible changes in the intelligence methodology.
output.research_lane: Agent-skill or procedural-instruction authoring: progressive disclosure, compact guidance, testability, evaluation, versioning, and reusable resources.
output.verified_practices: Agent skills should utilize progressive disclosure by pre-loading only metadata (name and description) at startup, loading full instructions only when triggered (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices). Skill descriptions must be written in the third person to prevent discovery errors and should include specific triggers for when the agent should activate the capability (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices). Procedural instructions should vary in 'degrees of freedom'—using high freedom for context-dependent tasks like code reviews and low freedom for fragile operations like database migrations (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices). Effective agent evaluation requires analyzing full execution trajectories and reasoning paths rather than just final outputs to identify systematic decision flaws (https://www.algolia.com/blog/ai/ai-agent-evaluation-frameworks-metrics-testing-strategies). The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes versioning using a YYYY-MM-DD string format to signal the date of the last backwards-incompatible change (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/learn/versioning). Reusable skill resources should be organized into domain-specific folders to keep the agent's context window lean and focused on relevant schemas (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills).

results.input: Adversarial review and threat-modeling practice for product and platform specifications: security design review, abuse/misuse cases, risk prioritization, and evidence-based severity assessment. Prioritize NIST, OWASP, and respected engineering guidance.

output.authoritative_sources: [OWASP Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Threat_Modeling_Cheat_Sheet.html) | [NIST SP 800-154: Guide to Data-Centric System Threat Modeling](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/154/ipd) | [PASTA Methodology (VerSprite)](https://versprite.com/cybersecurity-listings/devsecops/pasta-threat-modeling/) | [OWASP Risk Rating Methodology](https://owasp.org/www-community/OWASP_Risk_Rating_Methodology)
output.caveats: Threat models must be maintained as living documents throughout the lifecycle rather than being treated as one-time design artifacts. Quantitative risk scores are inherently subjective and require calibration against specific organizational risk tolerance to be effective. Relying solely on technical threat categories like STRIDE can lead to missing complex business logic abuses.
output.recommended_skill_changes: `clone-to-platform-pipeline` Implement a mandatory "Abuse Case Workshop" phase during the platform specification stage to identify potential business logic vulnerabilities before implementation. `dh-method-competitive-intelligence` Incorporate PASTA-style risk analysis to evaluate the security posture and attack surface of competitor platforms alongside their functional features. `skill-creator` Integrate a "Security Design Review" step that applies the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology to prioritize the hardening of high-impact agent capabilities. `clone-to-platform-pipeline` Add a requirement for Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs) to map trust boundaries and entry/exit points for every new platform component.
output.research_lane: Adversarial review and threat-modeling practice for product and platform specifications: security design review, abuse/misuse cases, risk prioritization, and evidence-based severity assessment.
output.verified_practices: Risk-centric threat modeling begins by aligning technical security objectives with business impact to ensure remediation efforts protect the most critical assets (https://versprite.com/cybersecurity-listings/devsecops/pasta-threat-modeling/). System decomposition using Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs) is essential for identifying trust boundaries, entry points, and data stores where attackers can interact with the system (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Threat_Modeling_Cheat_Sheet.html). Abuse cases serve as "anti-user stories" that describe unintended and malicious use scenarios to anticipate how features might be exploited (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Abuse_Case_Cheat_Sheet.html). Evidence-based risk prioritization requires calculating severity as a product of Likelihood (Threat Agent and Vulnerability factors) and Impact (Technical and Business damage) (https://owasp.org/www-community/OWASP_Risk_Rating_Methodology). Data-centric threat modeling focuses on characterizing the specific data of interest to apply fundamental security principles where they provide the most value (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/154/ipd).
